summary: xs-rs now implements PF_ACL_POSIX: -A/--acls parsing, ACL_CONFIG negotiation, access/default ACL record encoding and decoding after xattrs, validation before publication, and application on receipt. C++ xs and xs-rs carry ACLs in both directions, including no-op and ACL-only updates.
diagnosis: The work was protocol and metadata conversion, not throughput: Linux system.posix_acl_access/default values are exported to validated records and imported back to canonical kernel values, mirroring src/acls.cpp and put_acls/get_acls. Under -A the only added steady-state cost is up to two lgetxattr reads per inode; no transfer timing regression was measured or targeted for this metadata step.
change: Added rs/xs-rs/src/acls.rs with POSIX ACL read/write, record export/import, the C++ validation rules, and exact put_acls/get_acls codecs. Wired -A/--acls through cli, Options and HELLO advertisement; added ACL style refusals and ACL_CONFIG send/read in the C++ frame order; encoded ACLs after xattrs in DIR and DATA records; applied ACLs to files, FIFOs, specials and directories; and marked incomplete ACL metadata so existing destination files are preserved and the transfer exits 23.
expected_effect: A C++ client can push ACLs to xs-rs and pull them from it, and an xs-rs client can do the same against xs-c++, byte for byte. Invalid, incomplete, ambiguous or unnegotiated ACL data is refused before any destination file is created or replaced.
risks: Linux POSIX ACLs only: Darwin ACL_DARWIN/PF_ACL_UUID are explicitly refused, as on the C++ Linux build. ACL changes are not yet reflected in itemized output with an 'a' code, and --chmod ACL interaction is not implemented because xs-rs does not support --chmod.
tests: All four gate commands pass with XS_BIN set: cargo test (31 unit + all integration tests, including 2 new rs/xs-rs/tests/acls.rs interop tests), host clippy -D warnings, cargo fmt --check, and aarch64 clippy -D warnings. The parent's tests/acls_wire_test.py also passes 5 tests with 1 Darwin-only skip when XSYNC_TEST_BINARY points at xs-rs.
commit_body: Implement PF_ACL_POSIX: negotiate ACL_CONFIG, exchange validated access/default ACL records after xattrs in DIR and DATA frames, and apply them on receipt. Match the C++ ACL style checks, validation limits and incomplete-metadata handling so existing destinations are preserved on bad ACL data.
